contract: A23-91 server target hint: Swing / Release arg 1 = the client's pick (a monster Model). Valid only for a MANUAL attack and only when it is the Model of a monstersNear entry (alive, mine or nobody's, zone level gate, boss HitPad) within Range + HINT.Slack (2) and not hidden (rec._hidden / Model attribute Hidden). Valid: the aim follows it unless within HINT.KeepDeg (10 deg) of the facing, through a facing table only (the real root is never written; the no-pick A23-61 turn still writes it); monsters only (no player, no goose) only when the pick is outside the attack's AimCone of the real facing, inside it players and the goose keep the real front half (Around players too). Splash: centre = the pick. Multi: the pick first, then the nearest, no repeat. Around: the front half of the pick direction plus the pick itself even at Range + Slack (nobody else gets the slack). The queued manual swing keeps its pick; Q (ReleaseCenter Target) centres on the pick through SkillService (queued press too) or CombatService's fallback; a Self-centred Q ignores it. Anything else (wrong type, part, player character, dead / far / hidden / someone else's / gated monster, extra remote arguments, auto swings / auto Q) is ignored: the A23-61 swing of today.
limitations: The real client pick (HUD.PickTarget) and the network delay are not simulated (tools/test_auto_face.py covers the client). Splash keeps its blast radius around the pick, so a pick at Range + 2 reaches up to Range + 2 + Splash (as a pick inside Range always did). The IsA("Model") guard is redundant with the Model identity check and is not mutated. Root writes are seen as a new root.CFrame value (the combat world's CFrame.lookAt double); the real client's own turn is not simulated.
